Read images

Source: R/read-images.R
read_images.Rd

read_images() reads the metadata of microscopy image files and returns a long tibble with one row per image: one per file, channel, z-slice and time point. The img column holds lazy references to the greyscale images. Pixels are not read here; this happens when a montage is rendered, and only for the images it shows.

Usage

read_images(paths)

Arguments

paths

A character vector of paths to TIFF files (.tif, .tiff, .ome.tif) or to directories containing them.

Value

A tibble with one row per image and the columns:

  • filepath, series: file and image series (always 1 for non-OME files).

  • channel_index, channel: position and label of the channel. The label is the fluorophore if known, otherwise the channel name, otherwise "C1", "C2", ...

  • z, t: z-slice and time point of the image.

  • img: the image, a lazy greyscale image vector (see is_img()).

  • color: channel colour as a hex string, or NA if unknown.

  • channel_name, fluor: channel name and fluorophore from the metadata.

  • size_x, size_y, size_z, size_t: dimensions of the source file in pixels, z-slices and time points.

  • bit_depth: bits per sample (8 or 16).

  • pixel_size, pixel_unit: pixel size, always in micrometres.

  • z_step: distance between z-slices in micrometres.

  • meta_source, pixel_size_source: where the metadata came from.

Details

Because the result is a tibble, you select and process images with dplyr: filter() z-slices or time points, project a z-stack with summarise(img = max(img), .by = c(filepath, channel)).

Metadata are taken from the richest source available, recorded in meta_source:

  • "ome-xml": OME-TIFF (.ome.tif).

  • "imagej": TIFF saved by ImageJ / Fiji, including channel colours (LUTs) and channel names from microscope metadata carried over by Bio-Formats.

  • "tiff": plain TIFF. All pages are treated as z-slices of one channel.

The pixel size has its own source column, pixel_size_source, because scale bars need a pixel size you can trust. A pixel size from plain TIFF resolution tags ("tiff") is only used if the unit is centimetres.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
read_images("path/to/images")
read_images(c("ctrl.ome.tif", "ko.ome.tif"))
} # }
